title: Addition and Subtraction
questionReadAloudEn: What is addition? What is subtraction?
answerReadAloudEn: Addition means putting together two amounts to find the total. Subtraction means taking away or finding the difference.

title: Multiplication
questionReadAloudEn: What is multiplication? What is the multiplication version of five plus five plus five?
answerReadAloudEn: Multiplication means repeated addition of the same number. The multiplication version of five plus five plus five is three times five.

title: Division
questionReadAloudEn: What is division? What symbols show division?
answerReadAloudEn: Division means breaking a total into equal groups. Division can be shown with the division sign, a slash, or a fraction bar.

title: Operation Answers
questionReadAloudEn: What are the following called? Answer to a subtraction problem. Answer to a division problem. Answer to an addition problem. Answer to a multiplication problem.
answerReadAloudEn: The answer to a subtraction problem is the difference. The answer to a division problem is the quotient. The answer to an addition problem is the sum. The answer to a multiplication problem is the product.

title: Order of Operations
questionReadAloudEn: How do you solve a math problem with more than one operation? Example: parentheses, three minus one, times five, plus twelve divided by four.
answerReadAloudEn: Use the order of operations: PEMDAS. Parentheses, exponents, multiplication or division from left to right, addition or subtraction from left to right.

title: Powers of Ten
questionReadAloudEn: What does ten to the third power mean?
answerReadAloudEn: Ten to the third power means that ten is being multiplied by itself three times. Ten times ten times ten equals one thousand.

title: Common Conversions
questionReadAloudEn: One foot equals how many inches? One yard equals how many feet? One pound equals how many ounces? One liter equals how many milliliters?
answerReadAloudEn: One foot equals twelve inches. One yard equals three feet. One pound equals sixteen ounces. One liter equals one thousand milliliters.

title: Expanded Form
questionReadAloudEn: Write three thousand six hundred fifty-two in expanded form.
answerReadAloudEn: Three thousand six hundred fifty-two equals three thousand plus six hundred plus fifty plus two.

title: Long Division Steps
questionReadAloudEn: What are the steps to long division?
answerReadAloudEn: To do long division: divide, multiply, subtract, bring over.

title: Quadrilateral, Rectangle, Square
questionReadAloudEn: Describe these shapes: quadrilateral, rectangle, square.
answerReadAloudEn: A quadrilateral has four sides. A rectangle has four sides and four right angles. A square has four equal sides and four right angles.

title: Parallelogram and Rhombus
questionReadAloudEn: Describe these shapes: parallelogram and rhombus.
answerReadAloudEn: A parallelogram has four parallel sides. A rhombus has four equal parallel sides.

title: Volume
questionReadAloudEn: What is volume? How is volume measured?
answerReadAloudEn: Volume is the amount of space inside a three-dimensional shape. Volume is measured in cubic units, like cubic inches.

title: Rectangular Prism Volume
questionReadAloudEn: How do you calculate the volume of a rectangular prism?
answerReadAloudEn: Volume equals length times width times height.

title: Fractions
questionReadAloudEn: What is a fraction? What is the top called? What is the bottom called?
answerReadAloudEn: A fraction is a number representing a part over a whole. The top is the numerator. The bottom is the denominator.

title: Fraction Interpretations
questionReadAloudEn: What are the two main ways to interpret the fraction three fifths?
answerReadAloudEn: Three fifths can mean three equal parts out of five total parts. It can also mean three divided by five.

title: Mixed to Improper Fraction
questionReadAloudEn: How do we convert a mixed number into an improper fraction?
answerReadAloudEn: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and keep the same denominator.

title: Simplifying Fractions
questionReadAloudEn: How do you simplify fractions?
answerReadAloudEn: To simplify fractions, divide the top and bottom by the same number.

title: Multiplying Fractions
questionReadAloudEn: How do you multiply fractions?
answerReadAloudEn: To multiply fractions, multiply straight across.

title: Dividing Fractions
questionReadAloudEn: How do you divide fractions?
answerReadAloudEn: To divide fractions, keep, change, flip.

title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions
questionReadAloudEn: How do you add or subtract fractions?
answerReadAloudEn: Skip count by the denominators until you find a match. Skip count by the numerators. Add the numerators and keep the denominator.

title: Fraction Multiplication Size
questionReadAloudEn: Explain how you know that seven times four ninths is less than seven. Explain how you know that eleven times five halves is bigger than eleven.
answerReadAloudEn: If you multiply by a number smaller than one, you get a smaller number. If you multiply by a number bigger than one, you get a bigger number.

title: Decimals
questionReadAloudEn: What is a decimal?
answerReadAloudEn: A decimal is a shortcut way to write a fraction with a denominator of ten, one hundred, one thousand, and so on.

title: Decimal Place Value
questionReadAloudEn: Name all the place values in this number: six hundred seventy-nine and three hundred twenty-eight thousandths.
answerReadAloudEn: The place values are hundreds, tens, ones, tenths, hundredths, and thousandths.

title: Rounding Decimals
questionReadAloudEn: Explain how you round a number to the hundredths place.
answerReadAloudEn: Look next door. Five or more, up the score. Four or less, let it rest.

title: Adding and Subtracting Decimals
questionReadAloudEn: What is the first step to adding or subtracting decimals?
answerReadAloudEn: The first step to add or subtract decimals is to line up the decimal points.

title: Multiplying Decimals
questionReadAloudEn: When you are multiplying decimals, how do you know where to place the decimal point?
answerReadAloudEn: When multiplying decimals, count the decimal places in the problem. Use that number of decimal places in your answer.

title: Graphing Coordinates
questionReadAloudEn: Explain how you can graph coordinates, like three comma five.
answerReadAloudEn: Start at zero comma zero. Move to the right three spaces. Then move up five spaces. Draw a dot there.

title: Coordinate Plane Parts
questionReadAloudEn: Label the origin, x axis, and y axis.
answerReadAloudEn: The origin is the point zero comma zero. The x axis goes left and right. The y axis goes up and down.
